meta.ogDescription: Genuine George Carlin, taped January 1990 for the HBO special Doin' It Again. Transcriptions of that recording differ on the exact wording — "half of 'em" or "half of them."

answer.label: Spoken by
answer.sourceLine: Carlin taped this in January 1990; it reached television in the HBO special Doin’ It Again that June and record shops on the album Parental Advisory: Explicit Lyrics that November. Wikiquote files the line under that 1990 special ↗, not in the page’s Misattributed section. The exact wording is unsettled: the same recording is transcribed “half of ’em” on that page and “half of them” on Wikiquote’s Stupidity page, and we have not checked either against the recording.

source.heading: The 1990 stage performance

docMeta.dd: Doin’ It Again (HBO special) · Parental Advisory: Explicit Lyrics (album)
12–13 January 1990, State Theatre, New Brunswick, New Jersey
HBO special aired June 1990; album issued 20 November 1990 on Atlantic/Laugh
“Some People Are Stupid” — track 3, 2:28. Inferred from the title: nothing cited pins the line to that track, and Wikiquote files it under the special/album as a whole.

source.excerpt: Did you ever notice that, how many stupid people you run into during the day? … Think about this: think about how stupid the average person is, and then realize that half of ’em are stupider than that.
trail: Wikiquote’s Carlin page files this line under the work heading Doin’ It Again / Parental Advisory: Explicit Lyrics (1990) — and not in that page’s Misattributed section ↗, which holds the fake Carlin chain-letters. That page opens with a “needs additional citations” banner and this particular bullet carries no inline reference, so it records the attribution rather than vouching for a source.

Wikiquote’s Stupidity page ↗ cites the line more precisely, as “Carlin, George. (1990). Doin’ It Again [DVD]” at 00:22:09. It is a second Wikiquote page naming the same 1990 performance — the same project and editor pool, not an independent one — and it transcribes the wording differently: “Think of how stupid the average person is, and then realize half of them are stupider than that.”

The performance was recorded on 12–13 January 1990 at the State Theatre in New Brunswick, New Jersey ↗ and released as an album on 20 November 1990 by Atlantic/Laugh, drawn from the HBO special; track 3 is titled “Some People Are Stupid.”

HBO aired the special in June 1990 ↗ — the broadcast intro survives on the Internet Archive — and Carlin’s own official filmography ↗ lists both “1990 Doin’ It Again” and “1990 Parental Advisory: Explicit Lyrics.”

source.rightsNote: The line comes from a 1990 stage performance — the HBO special Doin’ It Again and the album Parental Advisory: Explicit Lyrics, issued 20 November 1990 — so it is squarely in copyright in the United States. Carlin’s estate enforces those rights actively: in January 2024 the estate and its executor, Jerold Hamza, sued over an AI-generated fake Carlin special ↗, alleging copyright infringement and violation of his right of publicity.

author.name: George Carlin
author.heading: About George Carlin
author.metaLine: 1937–2008 · American stand-up comedian, social critic & author
author.bio: Born in New York City on 12 May 1937, George Carlin spent five decades remaking American stand-up — from clean-cut 1960s television guest to the counter-cultural language obsessive of “Seven Words You Can Never Say on Television.” He recorded fourteen HBO specials between 1977 and 2008 and won five Grammy Awards, and by the 1990s his act had hardened into the bleak, precise misanthropy this line belongs to. He also wrote several bestsellers, including Brain Droppings (1997) and Napalm and Silly Putty (2001), and died on 22 June 2008.

misattribution.heading: Right name, unsettled words
misattribution.intro: This is not one of the fake Carlin quotes — the name on it is correct. What is unsettled is the exact wording, and almost nobody attaches a source at all.

items.who: “Think of how stupid the average person is, and realize half of them are stupider than that.”
items.why: Two transcriptions of the same 1990 recording disagree, so neither can be called the rewrite. Wikiquote’s Carlin page ↗ gives the contracted, doubled-up spoken form — “think about how stupid the average person is, and then realize that half of ’em are stupider than that” — while Wikiquote’s own Stupidity page ↗, citing the same DVD, gives “Think of … and then realize half of them.” The tidied version is the one that travels: it is the form Goodreads carries ↗, with nearly 2,000 likes. Settling which words were actually spoken needs the recording, not another wiki page.

The Quotations Page ↗ files it as a “Classic Quote” with no work, album or date, and Quotes.net ↗ gives the spoken-form wording with no source either. A real line with a real source becomes a floating slogan this way — and a floating slogan is what gets reassigned to someone else next.

Carlin is a heavy magnet for fabrications: Wikiquote’s Misattributed section ↗ lists forwarded set-pieces such as “The Paradox of Our Time” and “I Am a Bad American” as not his. This line is the opposite case — it sits in the quotes proper, under a named special, with a year.

misattribution.truthLine: He really said it, on stage in January 1990, and Wikiquote cites the special and a DVD timecode ↗. The name is settled; the exact words are not.

context.heading: Why this one stuck
lead: Carlin taped Doin’ It Again over two nights at the State Theatre in New Brunswick, New Jersey, on 12–13 January 1990. The bit this line closes is a straightforward complaint that there are too many stupid people and you meet them all day — it lands in the stretch where his act stopped being about words and started being about people.

The joke works because it dresses contempt as arithmetic. It sounds like a statistic, and it arrives with the cadence of one, which is exactly why it detached from the routine and went to live on coffee mugs. The Parental Advisory: Explicit Lyrics album that came out of the same performance in November 1990 even has a track titled “Some People Are Stupid.”
detailsBody: Pedants like to point out that the line quietly swaps the median for the mean: it is the median that has half the population below it, not the average. This is an observation about the joke rather than a correction anyone needs — the slippage is the gag. Carlin was not doing statistics, and the sentence would be worthless if he were.
context.pull: It sounds like a statistic. That is the whole trick.
